allowed_edges.rationale: Model exporters use shared tensor and metadata contracts.
Repository artifacts are produced by the model preparation workflow.
Triton loads versioned models and configuration from the model repository.
Serving metadata must match shared input and output contracts.
Deployment configures and controls the Triton service.
Deployment composes the metrics and dashboard services.
Deployment runs the benchmark tool in the pinned Triton SDK image.
The client calls Triton health, metadata, repository, and inference APIs.
The client uses shared request and prediction contracts.
The client records one structured history event per inference.
Log records use shared identifiers and prediction summaries.
Benchmarks reuse the public Triton transport and payload boundary.
Benchmarks consume a generated model-pair and tensor contract.
Perf Analyzer calls Triton inference and metrics endpoints directly.
Observability consumes Triton metrics and availability endpoints.

forbidden_edges.reason: Observability consumes metrics and must not import client implementation.
Shared contracts must remain independent of application code.
Shared contracts must remain independent of benchmark tooling.
The server boundary must not depend on its client implementation.
Model preparation must remain reproducible outside runtime orchestration.
Logging is a lower-level service and must not depend on its caller.
